**B01AF02** is the Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical (ATC) classification code for apixaban, a direct oral anticoagulant ([[doac|DOAC]]) used in the treatment of patients with [[atrieflimren]] [^src1]. As part of the Danish national clinical quality database for atrial fibrillation (Atrieflimren i Danmark, managed by RKKP), this specific drug code is integral to measuring and monitoring the quality of cardiovascular care across the Danish healthcare system [^src3]. 

In the context of clinical quality indicators, B01AF02 is explicitly listed among the approved codes for oral [[antikoagulationsbehandling]] [^src5]. It is grouped alongside other anticoagulants, including vitamin K antagonists ([[b01aa|B01AA]]) and other DOACs such as dabigatran ([[b01ae07|B01AE07]]), rivaroxaban ([[b01af01|B01AF01]]), and edoxaban ([[b01af03|B01AF03]]) [^src1]. The inclusion of B01AF02 in these coding specifications ensures that patients prescribed apixaban are correctly captured in national registries when evaluating indicators related to anticoagulation treatment and renal function monitoring [^src3].

A significant methodological shift occurred regarding how these treatments are tracked for quality measurement. As of January 1, 2023, the fulfillment of specific clinical indicators—such as patient education ([[indikator-4a|Indikator 4a]])—relies strictly on specific procedure codes (like the SKS code BFKB) rather than just the prescription of the drug itself [^src4]. Nevertheless, B01AF02 remains a foundational pharmacological identifier within the registry's methodology, linking individual drug prescriptions to broader systemic evaluations of treatment wait times, diagnostic follow-ups, and overall clinical outcomes for atrial fibrillation patients [^src5].
